messages.content: Western individualist values typically prioritize personal autonomy, individual rights, and merit-based authority, whereas many West African cultures emphasize communal harmony, collective responsibility, and lineage-based status. In these societies, group loyalty often supersedes individual rights, with social standing derived from one's contribution to the community rather than personal achievement. This contrast often leads to differing approaches in conflict resolution, where Western contexts may seek legal adjudication of individual grievances, while West African traditions frequently resolve disputes through restorative practices aimed at rebuilding social cohesion.
